A region in the $xy$-plane is bounded by the curve $y=2{cos}^{2}⁡x+{sin}^{2}⁡x,$ the $x$-axis and the lines $x=-\frac{\pi }{2}$ and $x=\pi ,$ as shown above. The area of the region is
worked_solution:
The area of the region is given by

$$
A={\int }_{-\pi /2}^{\pi }(2{cos}^{2}⁡x+{sin}^{2}⁡x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

Recall  ${cos}^{2}⁡x+{sin}^{2}⁡x=1,$ so we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}2{cos}^{2}⁡x+{sin}^{2}⁡x & ={cos}^{2}⁡x+({sin}^{2}⁡x+{cos}^{2}⁡x) \\  & ={cos}^{2}⁡x+1.\end{aligned}
$$

Here, we use the double-angle formula for cosine that involves the ${cos}^{2}⁡x$ term, given by

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡2x=2{cos}^{2}⁡x-1.
$$

 

Rearranging, we have

$$
{cos}^{2}⁡x=\frac{1}{2}(\operatorname{cos}⁡2x+1).
$$

Hence, the area of the region is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={\int }_{-\pi /2}^{\pi }({cos}^{2}⁡x+1)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-\pi /2}^{\pi }[\frac{1}{2}(\operatorname{cos}⁡2x+1)+1]\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{-\pi /2}^{\pi }(\operatorname{cos}⁡2x+3)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{(\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡2x+3x)|}_{-\pi /2}^{\pi } \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[(\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡2\pi +3\pi )-(\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(-\pi )-\frac{3\pi }{2})] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(3\pi +\frac{3\pi }{2}) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(\frac{9\pi }{2}) \\  & =\frac{9\pi }{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 15

A region in the xy-plane is bounded by the curve y=2cos2⁡x+sin2⁡x, the x-axis and the lines x=−π2 and x=π, as shown above. The area of the region is

a
5π2
b
9π4
c
5π
d
11π4
e
4π
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The area of the region is given by A=∫−π/2π(2cos2⁡x+sin2⁡x)dx.

Recall cos2⁡x+sin2⁡x=1, so we have 2cos2⁡x+sin2⁡x=cos2⁡x+(sin2⁡x+cos2⁡x)=cos2⁡x+1.

Here, we use the double-angle formula for cosine that involves the cos2⁡x term, given by

cos⁡2x=2cos2⁡x−1.

Rearranging, we have

cos2⁡x=12(cos⁡2x+1).

Hence, the area of the region is

A=∫−π/2π(cos2⁡x+1)dx=∫−π/2π[12(cos⁡2x+1)+1]dx=12∫−π/2π(cos⁡2x+3)dx=12(12sin⁡2x+3x)|−π/2π=12[(12sin⁡2π+3π)−(12sin⁡(−π)−3π2)]=12(3π+3π2)=12(9π2)=9π4.
